findings.title: A parallel epic's worktree changes never reach the main tree before its commit
quotes: It runs once (NFR-1) in the epic's tree with `EPIC_LIMIT = 1800` seconds
plus `worktree: <path>` when another epic is already claimed (FR-43)
patch, saved, err = land(root, slug, tid, tree, since_claim(lines, tid)[0]["evidence"]["commit"])
findings.fix: in CT-2, say that a worktree epic's changes are landed with `implement.land` before the commit, put back with `restore` and blocked on an apply error as `green` does, and that the worktree is removed after the commit.

sources.situation: the existing `green` applies a worktree task's changes to the main tree with `land()` (and puts them back with `restore()` if the review fails) before it commits on the main tree, then removes the worktree. CT-2's `finish` is modelled on `green` but leaves this step out. CT-3 stages only the main tree ("stages tracked changes outside the effort folder (`git add -u`)"), so the second epic of AC-44 would be tested in its worktree and then committed with none of its code.

findings.reason: CT-2 is "Like green" but names no land/restore step. CT-1 gives a second epic its own worktree (FR-43), and CT-3 stages only the main tree. implement.py `green` (line 756) calls `land()` for this, and nothing in the plan replaces it.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: Removing green leaves review with no caller, and the guard against edits to spec and plan files goes with it
quotes: `implement.red`, `implement.green`, `review`'s frozen-file check and `MODES` are removed
line = review(root, slug, task, lines)
`quickstart.md`, `architecture.md`) or `tasks.md`: a review fails on any change to them.
findings.fix: either have CT-2 run review's edits-to-plan-files check (PLAN_FILES) before the test run and fail the run on it, removing the rest of `review`, `closes` and `NEEDS`; or say in CT-5 that `review` is removed whole and in CT-9 that the card drops the line.

sources.situation: `review` is called only from `green`. CT-5 keeps `review` but deletes its only caller, and CT-2's finish never calls it, so it becomes dead code. Its check "the task edited ...: the spec, plan and tasks are not the worker's" stops running, and an epic agent that edits tests.md or contracts.md gets committed. CT-9 rewrites the worker card but doesn't say whether that promise still holds.

findings.reason: CT-5 removes only "review's frozen-file check". The edits-to-PLAN_FILES check in `review` (implement.py 582-583) is a separate part, and its only caller `green` is removed. CT-2 never calls review, and CT-9 says nothing about the promise.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: CT-16 reopens a dropped finding differently from the existing reopen code
quotes: only on a `dropped` finding; sets `status: open`, `validation: pending`, `ruling: <note>`.
f.update(status="open", disposition="", by="", note=f"{cid} was dropped; fix it in the plan or accept the risk")
findings.fix: write the ruling to `note` and clear `disposition` and `by` as `reopen_dropped` does, and handle `reopen` as an early branch of `_dispose_one` rather than a member of `DISPOSITIONS`, so it doesn't count as a disposition.

sources.situation: the existing `reopen_dropped` reopens a finding by clearing `disposition` and `by` and writing the reason to `note`. CT-16 puts `reopen` in `DISPOSITIONS` (whose other values all end a finding as `disposed`) and adds a new `ruling` key that `render`, `verdict` and the fix-check packs don't read. The human's words could then be missing from the ledger's rendered view.

findings.title: The epic's commit may leave out the new test files the flow just ran
quotes: the untracked paths the epic's tasks list under `Files:` or that sit under a listed folder
it must name every test file the epic's TCs cite
found = [f.split(":")[0] for t in task["own"] if t in tcs for f in re.findall(r"`([^`]+)`", plan.field(tcs[t], "File"))]
findings.fix: in CT-3, also stage the untracked files named by the TC `File:` lines the epic's tasks cite (`implement.test_files`).

sources.situation: the existing code finds an epic's test files from the TCs' `File:` lines, not from the tasks' `Files:`. A test file the agent creates that is named only in tests.md would be run and passed by CT-2, then left untracked by CT-3. The epic would close with its tests missing from the commit, and the pr gate's test-proof lens would have nothing to judge.

findings.reason: CT-3 stages untracked files from the tasks' `Files:` lines. CT-2 finds test files from the TCs' `File:` lines. Nothing ties the two, so a test file named only in tests.md can pass and stay untracked.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: An epic with an internal task dependency can never be claimed
quotes: whose tasks' dependencies are all done
whose dependencies are closed
findings.fix: say that only dependencies on tasks outside the epic count, and make CT-1 and CT-7 agree on it.

sources.situation: E-1 holds T-1 and T-2, and T-2 has `Depends on: T-1`. CT-1 picks an epic only when its tasks' dependencies are all done. Tasks are marked done only when the epic closes (`task_done` lines are written at CT-2 pass), so T-1 is not done at claim time. E-1 is never ready, and the claim says `no epic ready; E-1 waits on E-1`. FR-1 says "closed" and means other epics. CT-1 doesn't exclude dependencies inside the same epic.

findings.reason: CT-1 requires "whose tasks' dependencies are all done", and `task_done` lines are written only when the epic closes (CT-2). CT-7 only bans dependencies on later epics, so a task depending on an earlier task in the same epic is not excluded anywhere.

findings.title: The state table has no transition for an agent that hands back blocked
quotes: hand back `status: done` (no command needed) or `blocked` with a change request
unblocks a task blocked on a change request
findings.fix: add an event "agent hands back blocked" (claimed → blocked, cause change request) and the unblock outcomes for that cause to the table. Say whether this block counts toward the 3 runs.

sources.situation: an agent on claimed E-2 hands back `blocked` with a change request. The Epic table has only "agent hands back done" and "hand-back, tasks name no test" as hand-back events, and `blocked` is entered only by the 3rd failed run. The claimed epic stays claimed, or `implement.block` writes a task-level `blocked` line that CT-4's epic view doesn't read. Under auto, FR-47's "unblock a task blocked on a change request" has no epic state to leave.

findings.reason: The spec's Epic state table (spec.md 234-241) has no "agent hands back blocked" column, and `blocked` is entered only by the 3rd failed run. CT-9 lets the agent hand back `blocked` with a change request, so that path has no epic transition.

findings.title: The `PR fixes` epic has no tier and may name no test, so it can't be claimed or closed
quotes: `one_fix` writes no Tier, Effort or Mode
the confirmed findings become the closing `PR fixes` epic, which one implementation agent builds (CT-1)
THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to close the epic and say it has no test to run
findings.fix: have `one_fix` write the Tier, and say what test a PR-fix epic names, or allow the pr-gate fix epic to close without one.

sources.situation: a pr round confirms a finding about a doc or a card file, and `one_fix` appends `## E-n PR fixes` with no Tier line and a task with no `Test:`. CT-6's check requires a Tier on every epic, and CT-1 prints `card: nio-worker-<epic tier>`. The "no Tier line, approved before this change" fallback names old epics, not this one. CT-2 then refuses to close the epic with "no test to run". Under auto the one fix agent can never finish, and the run loops or stops on the pr gate.

findings.reason: CT-6 says `one_fix` writes no Tier or Effort, and `one_fix` today appends `## E-n PR fixes` with no epic Tier line. CT-6's check requires a Tier on every epic and CT-1 prints `nio-worker-<epic tier>`. The pre-change fallback names old approved epics, not this one. The "no test" part is weaker, because `one_fix` still writes a `Test:` line, but the missing Tier is enough.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

cherry-pick, without committing, #122's code commits
findings.fix: move the auto clause of CT-4 into CT-36, or state that it is built and tested in US-4.

sources.situation: the Build order puts CT-4 in US-1, but the auto flag and `who` come from CT-34 and CT-36 in US-4, which depends on US-1. When US-1 is built there is no auto flag to test. TC-47 sits under US-4 while its contract CT-4 sits under US-1. US-4 also applies the cherry-pick onto the code US-1 changed (`done`, `unblock`), where conflicts can arise beyond the three RF-37 names.

findings.title: `testing` can't be observed from history, so a second hand-back is not rejected
quotes: read from `claim`, `epic_test`, `blocked`, `unblock` and `task_done` lines
reject: tests running
findings.fix: write a `handback` line at the start of CT-2, or name the lock (`running.json`) as what makes `testing` observable.

sources.situation: CT-4 reads state from those five line kinds, and CT-2 writes no line when the hand-back starts, only when the run ends. A second `nio flow finish E-n` during the run sees the epic as `claimed`, not `testing`. The table says "ignore" for the hand-back, but CT-2 runs the tests again. That breaks NFR-1 (once per hand-back), and two runs write competing `epic_test` lines and failed-run counts.

findings.title: The revert can't see a live epic claim and names no way to release it
quotes: Rollback (migration flag): reverting the change restores per-task claims; an effort with an epic claimed at that moment needs its claim released first
if state["claims"].get("task"):
Writes one `claim` line `{"epic": "E-n", "tasks": [undone T-IDs], "commit": HEAD, "run"[, "worktree"]}` and `claims` `{"epics": {"E-n": {"run", ["worktree"]}}}`
findings.fix: Name the release step (for example `nio flow release <slug> E-n --by human`, or a documented manual edit). State what the old code does with `claims.epics`, `attempts["E-n"]` and epic-keyed `blocked` lines. Or make the new code also write `claims.task` so the old guard still refuses.

sources.situation: The change is reverted while E-2 is claimed and its agent is still writing code. The old `guard` checks only `claims.task`, so it lets a driver claim E-2's tasks one by one. Two agents then write the same files. The old `status` also skips `claim`/`blocked` lines that carry `epic` and no `task`, so an epic blocked after 3 runs reads as ready. The plan says the claim "needs its claim released first" but names no command. CT-2 releases a claim only on a failed run.

findings.reason: The old `guard` checks only `claims.task` (implement.py 283), while the new claim writes only `claims.epics`. The rollback decision says the claim is "released first" and names no command or procedure for it.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: Rolling back leaves tasks.md in a format the old code rejects
quotes: `FIELDS` becomes `Files, Serves, Test, Depends on, Parallel`
FIELDS = ["Files", "Serves", "Test", "Depends on", "Parallel", "Tier", "Effort", "Mode"]
"tier": tasks.TIER.match(f["Tier"]).group(1) if f.get("Tier") else ""
findings.fix: Extend the rollback decision to say how tasks.md written in the new format is handled after a revert (for example, keep a per-task Tier written by the drafter until the old flow is retired, or name the conversion step and whether it needs re-approval).

sources.situation: An effort's tasks.md is drafted and approved with `- Tier:`/`- Effort:` under each `## E-n` and none on its tasks, and then the change is reverted. The old `tasks.check` raises `T-n: needs \`- Tier:\`` for every task. The old `claim` prints `card: nio-worker-` because the tier is empty. Changing tasks.md to fix this means re-approving the tasks gate. The plan's rollback sentence ("reverting the change restores per-task claims") doesn't mention this file format.

findings.reason: CT-6 drops per-task Tier from FIELDS and moves it to the epic. The old `tasks.check` requires it on every task. The rollback decision ("reverting the change restores per-task claims") says nothing about tasks.md written in the new format.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: No test proves the rollback or a conversion with a live old claim
quotes: Setup: `impl()` with history: E-1's T-1, T-2 `task_done` under the old flow (their commits made); E-2 of three tasks with T-3 done.

Efforts already at implementing convert to per-epic at their next claim instead of finishing on the old flow, so no per-task code path survives FR-5 (FR-44): an agent call under the delegated grill (grill.md, OP-6), for the human's review at this gate; rollback is reverting the change.
findings.fix: Add a TC that converts an effort holding a live `claims.task` (and a `red` line) and asserts the outcome. Add one that releases an epic claim and checks the reverted guard against the new state.json/history, or state in the plan why the rollback needs no test.

sources.situation: The spec carries the migration flag. TC-43 is the only conversion test, and it only covers finished tasks with no `claims.task`, no `red`/`green` line and no wave worktree. No TC reverts, releases a claim, or checks that history and state written by the new flow are still readable by the old code. "rollback is reverting the change" is never tested.

findings.reason: The spec says "rollback is reverting the change", and TC-43 is the only conversion test. It covers only finished tasks and has no live claim or reverted code. No TC covers the rollback or a live old claim.
findings.note: fixed in the plan files; grill.md 'Plan jury round 1' logs each call

findings.title: Old wave claims and their worktrees aren't handled when an effort converts
quotes: An old `claims.task` is read as the claim of that task's epic.
mark = {"task": group[0]["id"], **({"wave": [t["id"] for t in group]} if len(group) > 1 else {})}
It runs once (NFR-1) in the epic's tree with `EPIC_LIMIT = 1800` seconds.
findings.fix: In CT-1, say how `claims.wave` and its worktrees convert: their work is merged into the epic's tree, the effort is refused until they are released, or the human is told. Add a TC for it.

sources.situation: An effort is mid-wave under the old flow when the change lands. T-4 and T-5 are claimed, and T-5's uncommitted work sits in `.nio/runs/<rid>/worktree`. CT-1 maps only `claims.task` to an epic claim and says nothing of `claims.wave` or its worktree. `finish` then runs and commits in the epic's tree, without T-5's worktree changes. Those changes are stranded or later removed. The old worker also can't hand back, because `nio flow green` is removed (CT-5).

findings.reason: CT-1 reads only an old `claims.task` as an epic claim. It says nothing of `claims.wave` or the wave's worktrees, which `claim` writes (implement.py 342). A converting effort mid-wave has no defined handling for them.

sources.situation: An in-flight effort's approved tasks.md has Tier lines only on its tasks. After the change, `nio check tasks` (and any guard or gate that re-runs it) may raise `E-n: needs \`- Tier:\`` against an approved file that can't change without re-approval. findings.title: TC-36's action never runs the evidence join, so its "no finding" assert is vacuous
quotes: - Action: `nio jury evidence S pr`.
- Binding: `src/nio/evidence.py:join` (existing)
Assert: the evidence lists `test_old` against AC-1; no finding `AC-1 has no passing evidence`; no fix task added.
evidence.join(root, slug, epic, "\n".join(found).splitlines(), results)
findings.fix: make the Action `nio jury evidence S pr --run R`, then a conformance output with `## Matches` holding `AC-1 -> tests/test_app.py:<line>`, then `nio jury collect`. Assert on `results["evidence"]` and the pr ledger.

sources.situation: `evidence.join` is called only from `jury.collect`'s `if impl:` block, using the conformance lens's `## Matches`. `nio jury evidence` runs the tests and the phantom and tamper checks but never joins. So with CT-27 left unbuilt, the action raises no `AC-1 has no passing evidence` finding and adds no fix task, and two of the three asserts pass. The bug it lets through: `join` still raising the blocker for an existing test the diff doesn't touch.

findings.reason: `evidence.join` is called only from jury.py:730, in `collect`. TC-36's action `nio jury evidence S pr` never reaches it, so "no finding AC-1 has no passing evidence" holds with CT-27 unbuilt.

findings.title: TC-40 points at an existing test that judges the implementation-E-1 gate, not the pr gate
quotes: - File: `tests/test_evidence.py:test_the_plan_holds_conformance_and_correctness_only` (existing)
lines, ok = jury.plan(root, "s", "implementation-E-1")
assert names == CORE_TWO, (names, lines)
findings.fix: make TC-40 a new test, for example `tests/test_evidence.py:test_pr_gate_runs_test_proof` (new). It should run `jury.plan(root, S, "pr")` on an effort at pr, assert `test-proof` is in the lens line, and check that `src/nio/agents/test-proof.md` holds `## At the pr gate`.

sources.situation: the named test plans `implementation-E-1` and asserts the lens set equals `{"conformance", "correctness"}`. Adding `test-proof` to `PR_CORE` (jury.py line 39) doesn't change that path, and leaving it out doesn't fail it. Because the test is marked `(existing)`, a builder keeps it as it is, and nothing runs `nio jury next S pr`. The bug it lets through: `PR_CORE` without `test-proof`, or a test-proof card with no `## At the pr gate`.
